trade: boat captain who carries the plantation's rice to Lilmoth
spot: at the plantation's north-east edge by the goats, waiting for a load
backstory: Reads-The-Shallows runs a flat boat that carries Hereguard's rice to Lilmoth, where big ships cannot come. She waits at the north-east edge of the plantation for the next load. She knows every channel between here and the walls and charges for each.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41 (lighters carry goods in); story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71 (Hereguard rice)
temperament: Brisk, practical and proud of her craft; impatient with landsmen.
manner: Clipped, nautical words; calls strangers 'passenger' and every place by how many turns of the channel it is.
wants: A full load and a fair wind before the plantation's steward changes his mind about the price.
grudge: The big ship's crew at the wreck to the south, who lost their vessel and still tell people she ran it aground.
notices: Weather, water depth and whether a stranger can sit in a boat without tipping it.
opinions: Thinks Lifts-The-Sacks is the only hand who loads properly; thinks the soldiers, Sees-No-Shade and Rakhee-Tul, guard the wrong side of the plantation; thinks Lilmoth Dock is a mess of small craft.
secret: She cannot read a chart and steers by memory and song.

trade: plantation hand who keeps the house's yard and stores
spot: in the yard by the plantation house on its west side, between the barrels and the benches
backstory: Hurz-Weel keeps the yard and the stores of the plantation house. He stands by the house because the steward wants a hand within call. He was born on the plantation and has never been further than Lilmoth.
lore: story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71 (Hereguard Plantation); story/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md:83
temperament: Dutiful, anxious and a little self-important; worries about everything he is responsible for.
manner: Fussy, repeats instructions back, calls strangers 'visitor' and asks if they have business at the house.
wants: The stores counted and right before anyone checks them.
grudge: The manor servants Folds-The-Linen and Mazei-Tul, who sit about while he does the heavy work.
notices: Who goes near the barrels and what they carry away.
opinions: Admires Looks-At-Books for her learning; resents Folds-The-Linen and Mazei-Tul; thinks Reads-The-Shallows overcharges.
secret: Two of the food barrels are short, and he has been eating from them.

trade: plantation hand and loader
spot: in the middle of the plantation among the goats and chickens, between the house and the workbenches
backstory: Lifts-The-Sacks loads the plantation's rice and does whatever heavy work is left. He stands in the middle of the yard because every job passes him. He is working off an owing of months for a debt his uncle ran up.
lore: story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:68-77, :97-99 (an owing passes with a household); story/lore/extrapolation/gap-register.md:145 (QA7, Owing gangs hired to Hereguard)
temperament: Cheerful, strong and resigned; refuses to be pitied.
manner: Plain short sentences and a laugh at the end; counts in nushmeekos; calls strangers 'friend' and talks to the goats more than to people.
wants: To finish his months by the next flood and go home to his tribe.
grudge: His uncle, dead now, whose debt he carries.
notices: Strength and posture; he can tell what a stranger has carried for years by their shoulders.
opinions: Likes Reads-The-Shallows, who thanks him; thinks Hurz-Weel fusses; is wary of the soldiers, Sees-No-Shade above all.
secret: He has counted his months himself and thinks the ledger has added three that he never owed.

trade: street seller of food and small goods to the plantation's hands
spot: on the plantation's east side near the cooking spit, where the hands eat
backstory: Salith sells food and small goods to the plantation's hands where they come to eat. She stands near the spit because hungry people buy. She came from Lilmoth to sell and stayed because the plantation has no other seller.
lore: story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71; census JobStreetVendorFaction
temperament: Motherly and blunt; scolds her customers and gives them credit.
manner: Warm, bossy, calls everyone 'hatchling' whatever their age, and ends with 'Eat something.'
wants: The hands to pay what they owe her before the next boat leaves.
grudge: The plantation's steward, who takes a cut of her sales for 'the use of the yard'.
notices: Who is thin, who is sick and who has not eaten today.
opinions: Mothers Okan-Wul; thinks Stares-At-Clouds is lazy and sweet; thinks Uleesh, who sells her fish, the most honest man outside the walls.
secret: She lets Lifts-The-Sacks eat free and writes his share on the steward's account.

trade: plantation hand who builds and mends the huts
spot: near Salith on the east side of the plantation, by the huts he keeps standing
backstory: Okan-Wul builds and mends the hands' huts on the plantation's east side. He stays near Salith's stall between jobs. He is young and wants to build something that will not rot in a season.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:42-45 (Argonian stilt building; Imperial houses sank)
temperament: Earnest, restless and a dreamer; full of plans, short on patience.
manner: Talks with his hands, starts sentences with 'What if', calls strangers 'stranger' and asks what buildings look like where they come from.
wants: Good timber and someone to show him how stone is laid.
grudge: The house, which gets dry stone walls while the hands get reed huts.
notices: Joints, rot, roofs and how a stranger's boots are made.
opinions: Thinks Salith is the plantation's real headwoman; finds Hurz-Weel a fusspot; admires the stone wall on the east edge more than anyone else does.
secret: He has been taking boards from the carpenter's bench at night to build a hut of his own.

trade: fisher of the shallows below Lilmoth's walls
spot: in the open water south of the walls, among the lily pads where the fish feed
backstory: Uleesh fishes the shallows below Lilmoth's walls and sells his catch inside. He lives outside because the rent inside is more than fish pay. He has fished the same water for twenty years and talks to it.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39 (shallow water); story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:29-31 (fish of Oliis Bay)
temperament: Content, superstitious and stubborn; nothing hurries him.
manner: Slow, plain sentences, often about the water as if it were a person; calls strangers 'dry-foot'.
wants: A good night's catch and nobody splashing about his lily pads.
grudge: The slaughterfish, which take his catch off the line, and the people who throw scraps that bring them.
notices: Ripples, splashes and anything that has been in the water; he can tell a swimmer from a wader.
opinions: Thinks the plantation at Hereguard pays its hands too little; buys his bait from Salith at Hereguard and likes her; thinks Lolmoth's walls keep out the wrong people.
secret: He feeds the old giant crab in the shallows to the south-west and believes it keeps the slaughterfish off.

trade: plantation hand who watches the flood water and the paddies' far edge
spot: at the north-east edge of the plantation, beyond the huts, where the water comes in
backstory: Stares-At-Clouds watches the water at the north-east edge of the plantation and warns when it rises. He stands out beyond the huts because the flood comes from there. He was sold on to Hereguard's labour from a broker in Lilmoth and does not know who holds his months now.
lore: story/lore/extrapolation/gap-register.md:145 (QA7: a Lilmoth broker hires an Owing gang to Hereguard); story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:90-96
temperament: Melancholy, gentle and absent; drifts off mid-sentence.
manner: Slow, fragmentary sentences with long gaps; calls strangers 'you' and asks what the sky looked like where they came from.
wants: To know who holds his months, so he knows who to pay.
grudge: The broker in Lilmoth who sold him on without telling him.
notices: Clouds, water level and birds; a stranger who comes from upriver.
opinions: Is grateful to Salith; thinks Lifts-The-Sacks too cheerful to be real; has never spoken to the soldiers and does not mean to.
secret: He keeps a knotted cord, one knot a day, and it no longer agrees with anyone's ledger.

trade: house servant at the plantation house
spot: by the plantation house, near the bed and benches on its south side
backstory: Folds-The-Linen keeps the plantation house clean and its linen folded. He stays near the house in case he is called. He takes pride in the house as if it were his own.
lore: story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71; story/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md:83
temperament: Prim, proud and secretly kind; looks down on the field hands and feeds them scraps.
manner: Formal, careful sentences, calls strangers 'guest' and talks of the house as 'we'.
wants: Visitors to wipe their feet and the meat barrels kept away from the linen.
grudge: Hurz-Weel, who tramps mud through the house.
notices: Clothes: stains, tears, cut and cloth, and what they say about the wearer.
opinions: Thinks Mazei-Tul is idle; thinks Looks-At-Books is the only person here worth talking to; disapproves of Salith, who feeds the hands on credit.
secret: He has tried on the house's best clothes in the dresser more than once.

trade: house servant who keeps the plantation's horses
spot: on the north side of the plantation house, close to the horses
backstory: Mazei-Tul is a house servant who has made himself the keeper of the horses. He stands on the north side because the horses are there and the work in the house is not. He would rather be a rider than a servant.
lore: story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71; story/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md:83
temperament: Lazy in the house, devoted in the stable; sulky until you mention horses.
manner: Mumbles, then talks fast and bright about animals; calls strangers 'rider' whether they ride or not.
wants: To ride the saddled black horse to Lilmoth and back without being missed.
grudge: Folds-The-Linen, who reports him every time he slips out.
notices: Mounts, saddles and boots with stirrup wear; how a stranger treats an animal.
opinions: Thinks Folds-The-Linen is a tattletale; likes Lifts-The-Sacks, who helps with the feed; thinks Lilmoth too crowded for a horse.
secret: He has named every horse and cow on the plantation and talks to them at night.

trade: headman of the marsh village south-west of Lilmoth Dock
spot: beside the village cooking spit, the middle of his people
backstory: Flaa Heet leads a handful of families who live on the open marsh outside Lilmoth rather than pay its rents. He stands by the cooking spit because that is where every quarrel and every catch ends up. He wants no seat on the merchant council and says so before anyone offers.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-66 (merchant council; elders settle quarrels); :39 (shallow water)
temperament: Patient and weighty; he lets a silence run until the other person fills it, and he decides slowly and does not change his mind.
manner: Speaks in short, complete sentences and often in 'we' for the village; calls a stranger 'walker' and ends a ruling with 'So it is.'
wants: A dry season for the stores and one more boat, so the children stop wading to the fish barrels.
grudge: The merchants of Lilmoth, who send collectors for a tariff on fish that never passed their gate.
notices: Whether a stranger's boots are wet to the knee (they came over the marsh) or dry (they came by the dock), and whether they look at the food barrels.
opinions: Thinks Tseeta haggles too hard and is good for the village anyway; is fond of Peeks-Under-Boats and pretends not to be; considers the sellswords on the shore track (Breaks-The-Oar's band) a fire waiting for dry grass.
secret: He keeps a tally of every favour the village owes and is owed, scratched on the underside of his chair, and he has never let one go.

trade: a hatchling of Flaa Heet's village who runs errands and gets under feet
spot: the north edge of the village, where he can see the boats and the path to the fish barrels
backstory: A hatchling of Flaa Heet's village, small even for his age. He hangs about the north edge because that is where the boats come in and where nobody tells him to carry things. He wants to be a boat captain and practises by bossing frogs.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41 (a harbour of small craft)
temperament: Bold, nosy and easily bored; he asks three questions for every one he answers.
manner: Talks fast in short bursts, repeats a word he likes ('huge', 'huge'), and calls any stranger 'big one'.
wants: To be taken out in the rowboat to the north-east, just once, without his mother knowing.
grudge: The fish barrels, because carrying to them is his chore and they smell.
notices: Weapons, boots and anything shiny; he will tell a stranger exactly what they are carrying.
opinions: Thinks Flaa Heet knows everything; thinks Hums-To-The-Rain sings too much; is scared of Deep-In-His-Cups and says he is not.
secret: He hid a pretty stone under the rowboat by the village and tells everyone he lost it.

trade: stall seller of food and small goods for the village
spot: at her stall on the north side of the village, the first stall anyone walking in from the dock meets
backstory: Tseeta sells the village's surplus to whoever walks in from the dock: fish, roots and small goods. She chose the north side so she meets buyers before Okeeh-Jas does. She is saving for a stall inside Lilmoth's walls and tells nobody how close she is.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41 (a boat-and-lighter trade economy); census JobStreetVendorFaction
temperament: Sharp, quick and competitive; friendly exactly as long as you are buying.
manner: Brisk, counts on her claws as she talks, calls strangers 'buyer' whether they buy or not, and closes with 'Good trade.'
wants: To sell out before the light goes, and to beat Okeeh-Jas's takings for the day.
grudge: Okeeh-Jas, who undersells her on purpose and smiles while doing it.
notices: A buyer's purse before their face; who looks hungry; whether coin is new.
opinions: Respects Flaa Heet but thinks he is too soft on debts; thinks Okeeh-Jas is a thief with a stall; thinks the Docks to the east are where real money is.
secret: She buys some of her stock from the thieves on the shore track and does not ask where it came from.

trade: net-mender and gatherer of the village
spot: on the west side of the village, between the spit and the second hearth, where the nets dry
backstory: Hums-To-The-Rain mends the village's nets and gathers what grows on the marsh. She works on the west side where the nets dry between the two hearths. She came from a tribe inland years ago and has never said which one.
lore: story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:108-116 (traits fade far from a tribe's Hist); story/lore/lilmoth.md:39
temperament: Gentle and dreamy, slow to anger and slow to answer; kind to everyone and close to no one.
manner: Soft, unhurried sentences, hums between them, calls strangers 'traveller' and says 'mm' when she agrees.
wants: Enough dry rope to finish the big net before the next rain.
grudge: Whoever cut a hole in her best net on purpose last season; she suspects Okeeh-Jas's hatchling cousin, and is probably wrong.
notices: Plants: what is ripe, what has been picked, and what a stranger has in their pack that grew somewhere else.
opinions: Thinks Flaa Heet carries too much alone; likes Peeks-Under-Boats and lets him tease her; thinks the marsh north of the village is kinder than Lilmoth's walls.
secret: Her colours have faded since she left her tribe, and she paints her frill with berry juice so no one asks why.

trade: stall seller of food and small goods, south side of the village
spot: at her stall on the south side of the village, near the boat landing
backstory: Okeeh-Jas sells food and small goods from the south stall, where the rowboat comes in. She trades with anyone who lands, and she likes the gossip as much as the coin. She married into the village and still talks like the city.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41; :46 (Pusbottom); census JobStreetVendorFaction
temperament: Cheerful, gossipy and shrewd under it; she laughs at most things, including her own prices.
manner: Chatty, long run-on sentences broken by 'you see?', calls strangers 'dear' and drops city slang.
wants: News: who came in, who left, who owes whom; she trades it as readily as fish.
grudge: Tseeta, who started the rumour that her fish is old.
notices: Gossip on a stranger's face: a fresh cut, a tired walk, a ring that does not fit.
opinions: Thinks Tseeta is too serious to be good at selling; finds Flaa Heet dull and wise; thinks Deep-In-His-Cups knows more than he lets on.
secret: She grew up in Pusbottom and left owing a moneylender there; she has never gone back through the walls.

trade: sellsword and brawler, the fists of a band of three
spot: at the band's camp on the shore track south-west of Lilmoth Dock, by the bedrolls
backstory: Breaks-The-Oar fights with his fists for whoever pays the band. He camps on the shore track with Heem-Tsal and Keeps-Both-Edges because the dock will not hire them and the city will not let them in armed. He is the one who talks terms.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-63 (council employs guards); :80-82 (foreigners kept to the docks once)
temperament: Loud, easy-going and quick to swing; holds no grudge longer than a bruise lasts, except one.
manner: Blunt and hearty; short sentences, cracks his knuckles mid-speech, calls strangers 'friend' and means 'customer'.
wants: Paid work for the band this week, before Heem-Tsal walks off to find better company.
grudge: The council's guards, who turned the band away from the dock gate for being 'unlicensed blades'.
notices: How a stranger stands: weight, reach and which hand they favour.
opinions: Trusts Keeps-Both-Edges with his life and his purse; thinks Heem-Tsal is cleverer than all of them and too proud; thinks Deep-In-His-Cups is good company and a bad debt.
secret: He has never won a fight against Keeps-Both-Edges and lets the band believe it was a draw.

trade: battle-mage of fire, the band's spell and its scholar
spot: a few paces from the band's bedrolls on the shore track, on the side away from the others
backstory: Heem-Tsal casts fire for the band and reads whatever he can get. He stands a little apart from Breaks-The-Oar and Keeps-Both-Edges because he finds their talk tiresome. He joined them for passage south and has not yet found a reason to leave.
lore: story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:65-66 (Xinchei-Konu, Ixtaxh Xanmeer); story/lore/lilmoth.md:110-116
temperament: Proud, curious and a little contemptuous; warms up at once to anyone who asks a real question.
manner: Long precise sentences, corrects people's words, calls strangers 'ojel' (non-Jel speaker) without malice, and says 'Precisely.'
wants: A look inside the silted Ixtaxh Xanmeer, and someone to carry the lamp.
grudge: The tree-minders of Lilmoth, who refused to let him sit by the city's Hist and take notes.
notices: Magic: a stranger's staff, the burn on their sleeve, whether they move like a caster.
opinions: Thinks Breaks-The-Oar is a good man with an empty head; respects Keeps-Both-Edges's discipline; has heard of Looks-At-Books at Hereguard and wants to see her shelf.
secret: He failed his trials at a mages' school and the robe he wears is borrowed from the one who passed.

trade: swordsman with two blades, the band's watch
spot: beside Breaks-The-Oar at the band's camp, facing the track so nothing comes up it unseen
backstory: Keeps-Both-Edges fights with a blade in each hand and keeps the band's watch. He stands facing the track so he sees anyone coming from the dock or the marsh. He was a guard once and will not say for whom.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-63 (council employs guards); story/lore/lilmoth.md:64-66
temperament: Quiet, watchful and dry; slow to trust and loyal once he does.
manner: Few words, often just a fact and a nod; calls strangers 'you there' and answers questions with questions.
wants: To get the band off this shore track before the dead come down from the walls one night.
grudge: The man who hired the band last and paid in promises; he has not said a name.
notices: Exits, the ground between him and a stranger, and whether their hands stay still.
opinions: Thinks Breaks-The-Oar talks too much and fights well; thinks Heem-Tsal will get them all killed for a book; keeps an eye on Waits-For-Lanterns by the leeks.
secret: He still carries his old guard token and takes it out when he thinks no one is looking.

trade: drinker and talker, of no settled trade
spot: sitting out on the shore track south-west of Lilmoth Dock, where the guards do not bother him
backstory: Deep-In-His-Cups was a lighterman once and is now mostly a drinker. He sits on the shore track because the dock guards move him on and nobody else does. He watches the dock all day and remembers more of it than he lets on.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41 (lighters carry goods from ships anchored out)
temperament: Maudlin and friendly in turns; generous with stories, mean with his bottle.
manner: Rambles, loses the thread and finds it again, calls everyone 'my good friend', and is the one Argonian here who slurs his words together.
wants: Another drink, and someone to listen to the story of the lighter he lost.
grudge: The lighter-master who sacked him for a sinking that was not his fault, he says.
notices: Who comes and goes at the dock; boats and their loading; anyone carrying a bottle.
opinions: Loves Breaks-The-Oar, who buys; is wary of Keeps-Both-Edges, who watches; thinks Okeeh-Jas the kindest seller on the marsh.
secret: He did sink the lighter, drunk, and has never said so sober.

trade: thief and scavenger of the dock's edges
spot: among the leeks on the shore north of the band's camp, close enough to the dock to watch it
backstory: Sheeh-Vos scavenges what the dock loses and steals what it does not. He crouches among the leeks so he looks like a gatherer to anyone passing. He works with Waits-For-Lanterns and does not like him.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:46 (the criminal underground); :62-63 (guards patrol)
temperament: Jumpy, greedy and sly; quick to smile, quicker to run.
manner: Whispers even when no one is near, talks out of the side of his mouth, calls strangers 'cousin' and says 'eh?' after a claim to see if it landed.
wants: To get to the bodies at the dock's east end before anyone official does.
grudge: Waits-For-Lanterns, who takes the larger share because he 'planned' it.
notices: Pockets, purses and locks; whether a stranger's pack is heavy.
opinions: Thinks Waits-For-Lanterns is a coward; thinks Tseeta pays fair for what she does not ask about; avoids Keeps-Both-Edges's eye.
secret: He has already taken a ring off one of the dead and is afraid it is cursed.

trade: thief who works the dark, a planner of small jobs
spot: a few paces east of Sheeh-Vos among the leeks, nearest the dock
backstory: Waits-For-Lanterns plans small thefts and waits for dark to do them. He stands nearest the dock, where he can count the lanterns and the guards between them. He thinks of himself as a professional fallen on a slow season.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:46 (Pusbottom, the criminal underground); :62-63
temperament: Cool, patient and vain about it; despises haste in others.
manner: Measured, almost polite; long pauses; calls strangers 'my friend' with a little bow and never says yes or no outright.
wants: A partner with nerve; Sheeh-Vos has none.
grudge: The Pusbottom fence who cut him off after one bad night.
notices: Light: where the lanterns are, where the shadows fall, who carries a torch.
opinions: Thinks Sheeh-Vos is greedy and will hang them both; thinks Breaks-The-Oar's band would be useful if they could keep their mouths shut; wants nothing to do with Flaa Heet's village, which watches its barrels.
secret: He is afraid of the dark water and has never once swum, which no Argonian he knows would believe.

trade: soldier in the Lilmoth council's pay who guards the plantation's south side
spot: on the south side of the plantation by a bench, facing the water and the shore
backstory: Sees-No-Shade is a soldier in the pay of Lilmoth's merchant council, posted to guard Hereguard's south side, where the rice is grown that Lilmoth buys. He stands facing the water because whatever comes, comes from the shore. He takes the job more seriously than it deserves.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-64 (the merchant council employs guards); story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71 and extrapolation/settlement-register.md:53,83 (Hereguard's rice, which Lilmoth buys)
temperament: Stern, rigid and humourless; believes in rules because they are rules.
manner: Clipped, formal orders rather than sentences, calls strangers 'citizen' and asks their business first.
wants: Nothing to happen on his watch, and to be seen to have stopped it.
grudge: Rakhee-Tul, who was given the easier post and sleeps on it.
notices: Weapons drawn or carried loose, and anyone walking where they should not.
opinions: Thinks Rakhee-Tul is slack; distrusts Stares-At-Clouds for staring; respects Looks-At-Books without knowing why.
secret: He is afraid of the giant crab in the shallows and keeps his post well back from the water.

trade: soldier in the Lilmoth council's pay who guards the plantation's south side with Sees-No-Shade
spot: a few paces north of Sees-No-Shade on the plantation's south side, nearer the yard
backstory: Rakhee-Tul is in the pay of Lilmoth's merchant council and guards the plantation's south side with Sees-No-Shade, where the rice is grown that Lilmoth buys. He stands a little nearer the yard where the shade and the gossip are. He took the post for the pay and has stopped pretending otherwise.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-64 (the merchant council employs guards); story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71 and extrapolation/settlement-register.md:53,83 (Hereguard's rice, which Lilmoth buys)
temperament: Easy-going, cynical and talkative; does the least he can and does it well enough.
manner: Wry asides, shrugs, calls strangers 'boss' and gives advice nobody asked for.
wants: His pay on time and an evening off in Lilmoth.
grudge: Sees-No-Shade, who reports him for sitting down.
notices: Who is new, who is in a hurry and who might be worth a coin to let pass.
opinions: Thinks Sees-No-Shade will have a fit one day; likes Salith's cooking; thinks the wreck to the south is full of things nobody has bothered to take.
secret: He has been to the wreck and taken a silver piece from it, and left the rest for fear of being seen.

trade: bookseller and seller of paper and writing things
spot: by the tables on the west side of the plantation house, where she keeps her books out of the rain
backstory: Looks-At-Books sells books, paper and ink from a table by the plantation house. She keeps to the west side, under cover, because damp ruins stock faster than thieves. She came to Hereguard because the house buys paper for its ledgers, and she reads everything she sells before she sells it.
lore: story/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md:83; story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:84-89 (the ledgers kept by estates); census JobMerchantFaction
temperament: Reserved, wry and exacting; warm only to readers.
manner: Precise, slightly bookish, quotes titles, calls strangers 'reader' and says 'Mind the pages.'
wants: A buyer for the four volumes of The Argonian Account together, not one at a time.
grudge: The house's steward, who buys ledgers from her and pays a season late.
notices: Ink on fingers; whether a stranger reads or only looks at pictures.
opinions: Finds Folds-The-Linen good company; thinks Heem-Tsal, the mage on the shore, will want her shelf and cannot afford it; thinks Hurz-Weel cannot read and pretends to.
secret: She has read The Lusty Argonian Maid more times than any other book she sells and blushes if asked about it.

trade: boat captain at the Docks east of Lilmoth Dock
spot: at the head of the Docks between the cooking spits and the north door, where boats tie up
backstory: Seeks-The-Channel runs a boat out of the Docks east of Lilmoth Dock. She waits at the head of the landing between fares. She chose the Docks over Lilmoth Dock because nobody here asks for a licence.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41 (small craft); :80-82 (licences)
temperament: Easy, generous and a talker; a born host.
manner: Big friendly sentences, tells you three places when you asked for one, calls strangers 'traveller' and says 'Easy water.'
wants: A fare to Alten Merihall, where the money is.
grudge: The bears in the hills to the south-east, which took her goat last season.
notices: Where a stranger is going; whether they need a boat and can pay for one.
opinions: Thinks Wades-Late is the best hand on the Docks; feels for Feldril Nethri and will not say so loudly; thinks Lilmoth Dock is all guards and no business.
secret: She ferries goods for the thieves on the shore track on moonless nights.

trade: seller of food and small goods at the Docks
spot: at the south-west side of the Docks near the houses, where people come out to buy
backstory: Ushaa-Mei sells food and small goods to the Docks' families and anyone who lands. She keeps to the south-west side, between the houses. She is the Docks' memory for prices and holds everyone to last season's.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41; census JobStreetVendorFaction
temperament: Dry, sceptical and fair; distrusts newcomers and trades fairly with them anyway.
manner: Short, flat statements and a sniff; calls strangers 'outsider' and prices by memory.
wants: The cows kept out of her stall.
grudge: Seeks-The-Channel, who brings in sellers from the coast to undercut her.
notices: Short weight, bad coin and anyone handling the goods without buying.
opinions: Thinks Seeks-The-Channel is too friendly to be honest; likes Plaits-The-Reed; keeps Little-Minnow out of the stock.
secret: She wants to leave the Docks and has never been further than Lilmoth Dock.

trade: a hatchling of the Docks
spot: in the middle of the Docks between the chairs and the cooking fire, where the grown-ups talk
backstory: Little-Minnow is a hatchling of the Docks who goes where the grown-ups talk. She sits in the middle by the fire so she hears everything. She wants to be a boat captain like Seeks-The-Channel.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41
temperament: Shy at first, then fearless; asks very serious questions.
manner: Whispery, careful sentences; calls strangers 'sir' or 'miss' because Ushaa-Mei told her to.
wants: To see the bears, from far away.
grudge: Chases-Cows, who scares the cows on purpose and blames her.
notices: Animals and faces; whether a stranger smiles back.
opinions: Adores Seeks-The-Channel; thinks Chases-Cows is a pest; is fond of Feldril Nethri, who carves her toys.
secret: She keeps a toy boat Feldril Nethri carved for her hidden from the grown-ups.

trade: reed-weaver of the Docks, maker of mats and baskets
spot: on the south-west side of the Docks near the houses, at her weaving
backstory: Plaits-The-Reed weaves mats and baskets for the Docks' families and the boats. She sits on the south-west side near the houses, out of the wind. She is a widow and talks about her husband as if he had gone fishing.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:42-45 (Argonian building of reed and wood)
temperament: Calm, sad and observant; kind in a quiet way.
manner: Low voice, sentences that trail off, calls strangers 'child' even when they are older.
wants: Good reeds from the south marsh, and company in the evening.
grudge: The sea, which took her husband.
notices: Hands, knots and craft; whether a stranger makes things or only buys them.
opinions: Likes Ushaa-Mei; thinks Wades-Late should marry; worries about Feldril Nethri, who is far from any home.
secret: She still sets a place at the table for her husband.

trade: a hatchling of the Docks
spot: at the north side of the Docks near the cooking spits, where he can reach the cows
backstory: Chases-Cows is a hatchling of the Docks and the reason the cows run. He hangs about the north side near the spits, where food falls. He wants to be a warrior and practises on cattle.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41
temperament: Loud, cheeky and fearless; never still.
manner: Shouts, boasts, calls strangers 'warrior' hoping they will show him a sword.
wants: To see a real fight, or at least a real sword.
grudge: Ushaa-Mei, who chased him off her stall.
notices: Weapons and scars; he asks about both.
opinions: Thinks Little-Minnow is a baby; thinks Wades-Late is the strongest person alive; is scared of Feldril Nethri for no reason he can give.
secret: He fell in the water last month and could not swim back, and Wades-Late pulled him out.

trade: dock hand who hauls and ties up for the boats
spot: on the south-east side of the Docks by the benches, where cargo is set down
backstory: Wades-Late hauls cargo and ties up boats at the Docks. He works the south-east side where loads are set down on the benches. He is strong, slow-spoken and owed money by half the Docks.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41; story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:135 (dock crews)
temperament: Steady, shy and stubborn; gentle with children and short with bosses.
manner: One-line answers, long pauses, calls strangers 'ojel' if they are not Argonian and 'kin' if they are.
wants: To be paid by the ship crew who left their cargo at the big ship to the west.
grudge: Whoever hired Feldril Nethri's months; it takes the paid work off free hands.
notices: Loads, knots and whether a stranger's pack is too heavy for them.
opinions: Thinks Seeks-The-Channel talks too much and is honest; fond of Chases-Cows; uneasy about Feldril Nethri and ashamed of being uneasy.
secret: He knows the chest by the big ship has never been claimed and has not opened it out of fear.

trade: Dunmer labourer at the Docks working off an owing of months
spot: at the north end of the Docks by the north door, kept apart from the families
backstory: Feldril Nethri is a Dunmer labourer working off an owing of months at the Docks. He stands at the north end because he is put there and is not welcome by the fire. He came to Black Marsh to trade, lost a cargo, and was assessed months he cannot see the end of.
lore: story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:68-77, :94-96 (owings extended by food); :135 (dock crews); .claude/skills/dialogue-write/voices.md (Dunmer history in Black Marsh)
temperament: Bitter, proud and exhausted; courteous out of habit and scornful underneath.
manner: Long formal sentences in the Dunmer way, calls anyone not Dunmer 'outlander' and himself 'a guest of this marsh' with a dry edge.
wants: To learn who holds his months, and how many are left.
grudge: The Argonians who assessed his debt, and the food they charge back to it.
notices: Ledgers, tallies and who is lying about numbers; he was a trader once.
opinions: Is grateful to Seeks-The-Channel and Little-Minnow; thinks Wades-Late an honest man who looks away; despises the Docks and respects its people.
secret: He knows his family's house once traded in Argonian slaves, and he believes this owing is the debt coming due.
